title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
summary:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine.
Participants in the study will be given the opportunity to rate responses to health questions from the app.
The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.
Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life.

summary:

The hack, Bonta said, "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability."
